messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Radically variable times per iteration
parts:
I'm trying out Stan on a hierarchical multinomial logit model using data from a discrete choice survey. Doing four independent runs of 5000 iterations each, I get the following times per iterations, from smallest to largest:

* 2.9 seconds
* 4.4 seconds
* 44.7 seconds
* 61.8 seconds

The last two are still running -- 1370 and 990 iterations so far -- after over 17 hours.

Why does the time vary so radically from one run to another? Is this expected?

Here's some info to give you an idea of the size of the data:

* 914 respondents
* 12 choice tasks per respondent
* 4 alternatives per choice task
* 35 covariates per alternative
* 5 respondent covariates
* the process is using about 190MB of memory

I've also attached the .stan file.

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Re: Radically variable times per iteration
parts:
It just got stranger. I looked at the traces produced by the two runs that finished, and they are all completely flat. None of the model parameters changes in the slightest from one iteration to the next. I'm guessing this means that every step was rejected. How is this possible? I thought that HMC was designed to make the probability of rejection low.

This problem has over 30,000 parameters, as it is a hierarchical model with each of the 914 respondents constituting one group. Is this just too large of a problem for HMC to handle?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Radically variable times per iteration
parts:
There's no inherent limit on the number of parameters (aside from the RAM limits of the machine), but if every proposal is rejected, that is bad and would usually suggest a mistake somewhere. Where there any "Informational Messages" warnings that a proposal was going to be rejected due to various reasons?

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Radically variable times per iteration
parts: There are certainly some problems where the performance of HMC is known to drop, but the variation in run times is far more indicative of problems with our adaptation routines during warmup. When a chain starts way out in a tail the adaptation can be too aggressive and lead to poor sampling. Try running with tighter initialization values -- on the develop branch you can specify init=x to produce random values between [-x, x].

messages.subject: Re: Radically variable times per iteration
parts:
Yes, there were two types of warning:

    inv_wishart_log(i): W is not positive definite (0)

and

    error in call to cholesky decomposition; require symmetric matrix, but found;
    x[0,9]=-1.#IND:0; x[9,0]=-1.#IND:0

There were a limited number of such warnings, all before iteration 10, so I assumed that meant that it only had problems in the first few iterations.
